subject: Draft: damages exclusion scenarios + cap interplay — decision ask
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <counsel@legalops.com>, Evan Grant <evan.grant@bluewaveanalytics.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@bluewaveanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: damages exclusion scenarios + cap interplay — decision ask

Hi Claire / Evan / Maya —

Thanks for the redlines on the MSA + Order Form. We discussed the damages exclusion options internally and want to surface three practicable paths so we can converge quickly:

1) Mutual broad exclusion: consequential/special/incidental/punitive excluded both ways; limited carve-outs for fraud, wilful misconduct, IP indemnity, and data breach; cap remains 12 months' fees for order form and $1M enterprise cap.

2) One-way exclusion (customer-protective): Redwood proposes one-way exclusion in customer’s favor (i.e., Redwood waives liability for consequential but customer retains rights) in exchange for a higher cap on certain service-impact claims (e.g., data loss) and a service credit schedule.

3) Tailored carve-out approach: mutual exclusion but explicit exceptions for (a) loss of customer data and regulatory fines (b) indemnity for IP and (c) direct outage-related damages up to a separate SLA cap; punitive/incidental remain excluded.

We attach a tracked draft (Redwood-BW-LOLI-draft-v3.docx) and a short matrix (exclusion-scenarios-summary.xlsx) that maps business risk to commercial remedies.

Questions for Bluewave legal:
- Which of the three high-level approaches is a showstopper for you?
- Is Bluewave able to accept a mutual exclusion if we carve out data-loss/regulatory/fraud/IP?
- If you insist on one-way exclusion, can we get a discrete SLA cap for outage/data incidents (proposed $3M or 18 months' fees, whichever is lower)?

We'd like to make a decision this week to avoid a stalled procurement path. Laura / Ben — quick internal ask: if Bluewave pushes for one-way, what’s the minimum commercial concession you recommend (credits, cap bump, escrow, other)?

Thanks —
Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: damages exclusion scenarios + cap interplay — decision ask

Nikhil / team —

Thanks for the clear matrix. Bluewave’s commercial/legal view: a mutual exclusion creates asymmetry with our downstream customers and would expose us operationally. Our negotiator preference today is option 2 (one-way in our favor) unless Redwood can demonstrate why mutual is required for your risk profile (technical reasons, reinsurance, or third-party dependencies).

We note the following items from your draft:
- Mutual exclusion + carve-outs are acceptable in principle but the devil is in the definitions — the term "consequential" must be defined narrowly and examples removed that sweep in foreseeable customer losses.
- Any mutual exclusion must preserve remedies for regulatory penalties that flow from Redwood’s handling of customer data.
- If Redwood insists on mutuality, Bluewave will ask for a materially higher SLA-based cap for service-impact claims and an explicit RTO/RPO schedule tied to credits.

Practical ask: can Redwood produce a short memo (one page) explaining why mutuality is more than contractual preference — what operational/insurance/legal constraints drive it? That will help our C-suite sign-off if you need parity.

Regards,
Claire Huang
LegalOps Counsel (outside counsel for Bluewave)
counsel@legalops.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <counsel@legalops.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Grant <evan.grant@bluewaveanalytics.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@bluewaveanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: damages exclusion scenarios + cap interplay — decision ask

Claire / team —

Appreciate the candid feedback. Short version from legal ops at Redwood: mutual exclusion is our standard for two reasons — (1) parity with our downstream SaaS customers reduces moral hazard and helps with our insurer underwriting; (2) we operationally route many requests across third-party infra and can't selectively accept broader exposure for one counterparty without systemic consequences. That said, we want to find a workable middle ground.

Suggested compromise (redline included in v3):
- Keep mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages.
- Carve out (mutual): fraud/wilful misconduct; IP indemnity; regulatory fines arising from a party's breach of security obligations; direct data loss (defined narrowly).
- Introduce an SLA Damage Bucket: for outage/data-incidents specifically tied to Redwood's fault, direct damages recoverable up to an SLA cap of $2.5M (or 12 months' fees for the affected Order Form), with a defined credit schedule in the Order Form; these are not duplicative of the general cap.
- Define "consequential" to exclude lost profits only where they are not arising from a direct outage of Redwood services (adds clarity for both sides).

Why this works: it keeps punitive/incidental out (our insurers require this), preserves customer protections for real operational harms (data loss/regulatory), and creates a predictable commercial remedy set instead of open-ended one-way exposure.

If Bluewave insists on one-way exclusion language, the minimum concession I recommend is: (a) a $3M SLA cap for outage/data events, (b) extended data retention support at no cost for transition, and (c) enhanced incident response SLAs (faster engagement and root-cause reporting).

Attaching a tracked snippet of the exact clause we propose (see docx). Happy to hop on a quick call with Evan / Maya to walk the table.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Evan Grant <evan.grant@bluewaveanalytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Huang <counsel@legalops.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@bluewaveanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: damages exclusion scenarios + cap interplay — decision ask

Laura / Nikhil —

Thanks for the memo and the alternative. We reviewed with procurement and execs this morning. Bluewave is willing to accept a mutual exclusion only if the SLA Damage Bucket is plainly non-duplicative and the $2.5M figure is increased to $3.5M (or 18 months' fees) — our systems are customer-facing and a multi-hour outage has outsized downstream impact.

We also need clearer language on the definition of "direct data loss" — we propose "loss of customer data resulting exclusively from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct" and a 180-day window for claims tied to a particular incident.

If Redwood can accept those two edits, Bluewave can sign off and proceed to PO. If not, we'll need to escalate to procurement for a parallel vendor evaluation.

Appreciate the cadence here — happy to lock a short call if it helps.

Evan
VP, Commercial Ops | Bluewave Analytics
evans.grant@bluewaveanalytics.com
